title: What happened
sub: he comido, has visto, ya, todavía no
can: Say what you have done today, this week or ever, with he, has, ha + a verb ending in -ado or -ido.
doneText: You can now say what you've done today and this week, the way Spain does.

skills.haber: He, has, ha: the forms of haber
skills.irregular-pp: The odd ones: hecho, visto, dicho
skills.pp-spain: Today and this week: he comido

discover.intro: Both colours use the same verbs. Look at how the blue ones are built.

groups.label: Already happened
lines: Esta mañana he visto a mi amiga.
I saw my friend this morning.
We've worked a lot this week.

discover.question: How does Spanish build the blue sentences?
options: A small verb (he, hemos) and then the verb ending in -ado or -ido.
It changes the first letter of the verb.
It puts yo or nosotros in front.
discover.nudge: Not quite. Find the word just before comido, visto and trabajado.
discover.reveal: This is the pretérito perfecto, for things you have done. A form of haber (he, has, ha…) plus the verb with -ado (-ar verbs) or -ido (-er and -ir verbs):

hooks.title: When Spain uses it
rows: I've worked a lot this week.

learn.title: What you have done
learn.sub: Tap any row to hear it

blocks.text: -ar verbs take -ado, -er and -ir verbs take -ido. Only he, has, ha changes with the person. The -ado form stays the same: he comido, ha comido, hemos comido.

Spain uses he comido for anything in a time that isn't over yet: today, this morning, this week, this year, or ever. Hoy he comido paella. Much of Latin America says comí instead. You'll hear both, but this is how Spain says it.

blocks.title: Ya or todavía no
blocks.note: Ya means already. Todavía no means not yet. Both go before he, has, ha.

blocks.text: Nothing goes between he and the -ado form. No, ya and nunca go in front: no he comido, ya he comido, nunca he estado en Asia.
Perder (to lose) is the one for a lost bag or phone when you travel: he perdido el móvil (I've lost my phone).

enAlts: I haven't had anything to eat yet.
Have you ever been to Seville?
I've done a lot of work today.
I have worked a lot today.
Have you seen the cathedral yet?
What have you been doing today?
I have never been to Asia.

exercises.why: Yo: he. He comido means I have eaten.

items.blank: Mi padre ha sal___ de casa.
items.full: Mi padre ha salido de casa.

exercises.say: Esta mañana he perdido el móvil.
options: I lost my phone this morning.
I'm going to lose my phone.
I found my phone this morning.
exercises.why: He perdido: I've lost. Perder means to lose.
Hacer is one of the odd ones: hecho, not hacido.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.why: Ver is one of the odd ones: visto.
Ya goes before he: ya he comido.
Mis padres is they: han llegado.

exercises.prompt: Tap the word that is wrong.
exercises.why: Comer is an -er verb, so -ido: comido.
Ver is one of the odd ones: visto. Has for tú, ha for usted.

exercises.prompt: In Spain, how do you usually say "I had paella today"?
exercises.why: Spain uses he comido for anything that happened today.
Perder: perdido. In Spain it's el móvil.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Write a short message to a friend about your day: three things you have done today and one thing you haven't done yet.
write.starter: Hoy he…  También he…  Todavía no he…
write.model: Hoy he visitado la catedral y he comido tapas con unos amigos. Por la tarde he hecho la compra. Todavía no he llamado a mi madre.
checklist: He, has, ha + -ado or -ido: he visitado, he comido
The odd ones: hecho, visto, dicho
Todavía no for something not done yet

boss.title: Lost property at Atocha
boss.persona: You are Rubén, a patient lost-property officer at Atocha station in Madrid. The learner has lost a backpack. Ask what has happened, where they have been today, whether they have looked for it, and whether their name is on it. Use usted, and switch to tú if the learner does. Speak European Spanish.

choices: He perdido la mochila.
Ha perdido la mochila.
Ha is he, she or usted. About yourself: he perdido.
He perdo la mochila.
Perder is an -er verb, so -ido: perdido.

turns.en: Oh dear. Where have you been today?
choices: He estado en el museo y en un café.
Estoy estado en el museo y en un café.
Have been is he estado. Estoy means I am.
He estada en el museo y en un café.
The -ado form never changes: estado.

turns.en: And have you looked in the café?
choices: Sí, ya he mirado, pero no está.
Sí, he ya mirado, pero no está.
Ya goes before he: ya he mirado.
Sí, ya he mirando, pero no está.
Have looked is he mirado, with -ado.

turns.npc: ¿Ha escrito su nombre en la mochila?
turns.en: Have you written your name on the backpack?
choices: Sí, he escrito mi nombre dentro.
Sí, he escribido mi nombre dentro.
Escribir is one of the odd ones: escrito.
Sí, ha escrito mi nombre dentro.
Ha is he, she or usted. About yourself: he escrito.

boss.closing: ¡Aquí está! Una mochila con su nombre. ¡Buen viaje!
boss.closingEn: Here it is! A backpack with your name in it. Have a good trip!
boss.chatOpening: ¿Y qué más ha hecho hoy en Madrid?
boss.chatOpeningEn: And what else have you done in Madrid today?
